utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. President, Your Honours, we have a witness, his name is Ekrem Mahmutovic, and he will give us some information about facts which took place in the town of Vares and the village of Stupni Do in 1992 and 1993. Mr. Mahmutovic will, in the course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The solemn declaration; let the witness take that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honour, as I was saying, Mr. Mahmutovic will tell us about events in the town of -- in the municipality of Vares in the village of Stupni Do in 1992 and 1993, and in his testimony he will give us the names of seven localities which are on the maps that we have here. Before he begins his testimony, I should like to show the witness two maps which were prepared to this effect and on which he will be able to indicate various localities that he refers to in his testimony. These are exhibit pieces Z26124 and 26125, which I want to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, you have before you two maps, and on these two maps, beginning by the larger one, 2612,4, will you please point at various localities that we shall talk about -- and that you mentioned in your statement, too -- but first show us, where is Vares on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Do we have it on the map? Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you indicate it, please? Could you please show us where Vares is on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness says nothing.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we also shall be talking about Strijezevo.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Vares, on the map, is north-east of Sarajevo, on the road Sarajevo/Vares/Olovo, 50 kilometres or thereabouts away from Sarajevo, at the foothills of the mountain Zvijezda.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us where is Strijezevo? I'm sorry if I'm not pronouncing it properly, but could you tell us where that place is?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Strijezevo is to the south-west of Vares, on the right-hand side of the road, Sarajevo/Vares, about 13 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us where the locality of Dabravine is?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Dabravine is on the Sarajevo/Vares road, 14 kilometres away from Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Will you also please show us the locality called Pajtov Han.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Pajtov Han is 7 kilometres from Vares on the Sarajevo/Vares road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And will you now show us the town of Kiseljak, please, in relation to Vares.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The town of Kiseljak is to the south-west of Vares. I wouldn't know the exact distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Will you now take the second map, just for a moment, and indicate on this map the locality of Brgule, a place which is called Brgule, on the second map.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's not Brgule. I'm sorry. It's -- Brgule, it is about 20 kilometres from Vares, and it is practically east of the town, from the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And could now show us Stupni Do, the village of Stupni Do, and tell us, where is it in relation to Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Stupni Do is to the left of the Sarajevo/Vares road. It is two and a half kilometres away from Vares Majdan, and it is to the south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecutor please speak into the microphone? We can barely hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Now that we've established geography, if I may say so, Mr. Mahmutovic, we shall now turn to information that you can give us and which derives from your statement given to the Prosecutor's office on the 3rd of December, 1992, and in view of the changes in your statement which you made after the written statement. So I shall be referring to the summary of your statement in order to get precise, concise answers, and if I need any additional information as to it, then I will ask you to amplify on your answers. Mr. Ekrem Mahmutovic, you were born in 1950 in the municipality of Breza; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: In the area of the municipality of Breza, in a village there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. You studied political sciences in Sarajevo for two years, and after that, did your military service in the school for artillery officers in Zadar; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did serve -- yes, I did serve my military service in the school for reserve officers, artillery, anti-aircraft, in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And after that, you returned to Vares, and you worked in a mine first because Vares is a mining town, and then you began working for a company manufacturing optical devices; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Then, in April 1992, you were appointed a commander of a reconnaissance unit of the joint defence in Vares; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. In 1992, I was appointed the commander of the reconnaissance unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Then, in July 1992, you were appointed the commander of the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Upon the orders of the head of the staff of the municipality, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, I was appointed the commander of the Territorial Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. You left the army with the rank of captain of the first class, is that so, in 1995?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You have been living in Vares since 1961?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I've lived in Vares since 1961.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You are now consultant for defence matters with the Vares police; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You were a member of the SDP, that is, the Social Democratic Party, and now you are the vice-president of an ethnically-mixed party which is called Zabih in Vares, and you are its vice-president now, are you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct. I am the vice-president of the party for Bosnia-Herzegovina, its subsidiary in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Now, after this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Excuse me. Could the witness tell us what does "Zabih" mean? Could the witness please tell us what "Zabih" means exactly? Could you please explain what "Zabih" means or what is the programme of the Zabih party?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: This is the party for Bosnia-Herzegovina. "Za" means "for". "Bih" is "Bosnia-Herzegovina". The party was founded two years ago. It is headed by Mr. Haris Silajdzic. The party has its programme, and it made me decide to join the party, and that is a struggle for Bosnia-Herzegovina, such as it is within its nationally-recognised borders. That is, that all those who left their homesteads can go back to the places they left and to achieve coexistence in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: So "Zabih" means "for Bosnia-Herzegovina". This is the interpreter's explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Now let us go back to events which took place in Vares, that is, the municipality of Vares, after the elections of 1990. The census which took place in 1991 tells us that in Vares, there were about 22.000 inhabitants, of whom about 40 per cent were Catholics, 30 per cent were Bosnian Muslims, and about 19 per cent were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: This is a fact deriving from the 1991 census, and that's what it is. It was published in statistical documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: That election which took place towards the end of 1990, it was the SDP, the Socialist Democratic Party, which won the largest number of seats. SDZ, the Croat Democratic Union, ranked second, and the SDA, the Muslim party, came third; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That was the order on this, SDP, HDZ, SDA, and there was also UBSD. But the rest of them are negligible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: After these elections, the offices were distributed in accordance with the results achieved by these three parties, so that the mayor who was elected at the time was a Croat, who was a member of the SDP and whose name was Dario Andrijevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Dario Andrijevic was, on the basis of the ethnicity, that is, on the basis of the majority in the SDP, was elected the mayor of Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the same fashion, the commander of the Territorial Defence, at that time when it was joint in Vares at the time, was also another Croat but also a member of the SDP?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The relations following these elections in 1991 and 1992, the relations I mean among individual ethnic groups, what would you call them; good, harmonious, or how were they?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I think they were remarkably good.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At the end of March 1992, the commander of the Territorial Defence, a joint body that we have just mentioned, a Croat from the SDP was replaced by Mr. Borivoje Malbasic, who was another Croat coming from the same SDP party but who, according to what you said, was more open to the nationalist Croatian party, the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: There is a dispute about this. The witness's conclusion about why this politician was replaced, his purpose, this is a pure political analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, there being dispute about it, Mr. Lopez-Terres, you had better deal with it in a non-leading form.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Borivoje Malbasic was a member of the SDP, Mr. Mahmutovic, was he not?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I know that he was officially a member of the SDP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Being a member of the SDP, did Mr. Borivoje Malbasic have ideas close to the Croatian HDZ party?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't really talk about his feelings and ideas, but I do know that he was a member of the SDP, and that as a member of the SDP, he was appointed to the position of command of the Territorial Defence for the simple reason given that the previous commander of the Territorial Defence did not fulfil all his duties properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The appointment of Mr. Malbasic, was that done with the consent and approval of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the period that followed the appointment of Mr. Malbasic, the HVO started to form its own military forces, these being separate from the Territorial Defence forces which were joint until then, and these forces started to carry specific insignia with the red and white characteristic marks?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly the way you just said, there was a gradual separation between units of the Territorial Defence. Within the units, some carried the checker board insignia and others carried insignia on their left arms with the word "Vares" written on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You were able to note, in the same period, that the HVO forces were receiving new uniforms, new equipment, weapons and materiel, whereas at the same time you were able to note that the Territorial Defence was receiving nothing and had difficulty in obtaining food even; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. That is the way I saw it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The HVO forces also started parading with their weapons in the streets of Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What was the effect of these parades on the local population, particularly on the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Simply, the impression was that the HVO forces were trying to make a show of force and to demonstrate that force in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At the beginning of May 1992, the same person, Borivoje Malbasic, gave an order in which he decided to change the name of the headquarters of the joint Territorial Defence, which became the operational headquarters, and then the HVO headquarters itself became autonomous. It was moved and established three kilometres from Vares in a hotel called Ponikve?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) If I may, my learned colleague is exaggerating with these leading questions. He has said everything. He doesn't leave the witness the opportunity to say anything. I would suggest that questions be put to the witness rather than the questioning being done in this leading manner. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Naumovski, is there any dispute about this? It sounded to be quite a straightforward matter of fact. Is there a dispute that the HVO headquarters was in a hotel; is that in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I'm not disputing that fact. I am just asking that the witness be questioned in a way that is appropriate and why he has come. We agreed to leading questions with regard to general personal data, but these are other matters, particularly so as in the introduction the Prosecutor said that the witness has certain changes to make in relation to his previous testimony. The Defence is not aware of those changes, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, the point is this: If there's no dispute about these matters, if they are straightforward matters of fact such as a headquarters being in a particular building, what is the point of not leading the witness to those facts? If there are facts in dispute, then of course it's a different matter, but we are wasting time if there is no dispute about these matters. Mr. Lopez-Terres, when you get to controversial matters, would you please see, of course, that you don't lead. So any matters about the accused or anything of that sort, don't lead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Naumovski, I think that we agreed with you and the Prosecutor that we should apply this method of work. We are not going to re-discuss the issue every time. We're going to ask you for your cooperation so that this trial may be conducted in the fairest possible manner but also in the most effective and expeditious manner, and you agreed to that. Regarding the method, we agreed on it, but of course if there is a controversial issue, then you may raise an objection. You should not object in principle, because we have already reached an agreement on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: To the establishment of the HVO in a separate headquarters, the HDZ and the HVO of Vares established a military police unit consisting of some 40 members. All were very well equipped and well paid; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: This unit received orders from a person whose name was Zvonko Duznovic who you described --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think now we're getting to matters where you shouldn't lead. I suspect they will be matters of controversy. So if you would just ask the witness about Mr. Duznovic, who he was and any relevant matter about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Judge, may I enquire, because I'm frankly lost, do you have the Prosecutor's summary that we were handed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm on paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you talk to us about Mr. Zvonko Duznovic and any links that he may have had with the military police units that we have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Zvonko Duznovic is my colleague from the iron works in Vares. We worked together, and after the war broke out within the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and after he joined the HDZ, he was appointed also to the post of security officer in the Territorial Defence headquarters formed at the end of March in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Was he a highly-committed member of the HDZ, a prominent militant member?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I know that whatever he set out to do, he carried out completely, and the orders that he received, I don't know who from, he carried out them conscientiously, together with the police that he used to carry out his tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did Mr. Duznovic have an influence over that military police unit?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Duznovic did have influence over that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What were the actions undertaken by that military police unit in the town of Vares after it was established?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Having been established, the first operation after training carried out by that unit was an attack on a Serbian village called Planica, then also full control over the municipality of Vares municipality, the setting up of checkpoints at all exits from Vares municipality which were manned and controlled by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You indicated that Mr. Duznovic was a person with authority and conviction. This authority and conviction, was it exercised also over Mr. Borivoje Malbasic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Whatever I said, I abide by, and that is so, the way you said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us about a conversation that you had one day with Mr. Borivoje Malbasic regarding the activities and role of Zvonko Duznovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: May it please the Court, this is absolute hearsay and irrelevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You know, Mr. Stein, this isn't a trial in a municipal jurisdiction where you have a jury to protect and it may be that there are frequent interruptions. This is a trial before an International Court with professional judges. You know also that the rule against hearsay doesn't apply here. It would be sensible to allow this witness to give his evidence without constant interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: I accept that, Judge, but my problem is, frankly, the relevance of all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, let us be the judges of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Very good, Sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we could deal with this fairly rapidly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you report on the conversation that you had with Mr. Malbasic one day, quickly, in a few words?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Upon orders from Mr. Malbasic, I was commander of a reconnaissance unit of the Territorial Defence, and according to the chain of command, I was accountable to him. Upon my request that my soldiers should not be harassed in town, that their weapons should not be taken away from them, that they could move freely, that they could go home to have a bath and change, he said he could do nothing about it because Zvonko Duznovic was not obeying his orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: This influence of Mr. Duznovic, did it reach the president of the HDZ at the time, Mr. Ante Pejcinovic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The same relationship, in my view, existed between Ante Pejcinovic and Zvonko Duznovic as between Borivoje Malbasic and Zvonko Duznovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you hear Mr. Duznovic holding speeches that were hostile in relation to the Muslims on Radio Vares?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just ask the witness what Mr. Duznovic said. Can you tell us that, please, Mr. Mahmutovic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I shall try to quote what was occasionally stated on Radio Vares, and that was that Vares was Croatian, that it would remain Croatian, and that there could be no existence with other peoples within the territory of Vares municipality because only Croats should live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: This type of statement, was it repeated in other ways, in everyday life? Particularly, did you see posters with similar messages?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: In public places, posters were hung up, in places used for information, with proclamations calling Croats to unite, to defend their compactness, saying that Vares was theirs, and that they must live in Vares, and that there could be no coexistence with other peoples who used to live in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were you informed during June 1992 that the HDZ and the HVO were planning to take over power in Vares on the 15th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. I was informed that this event was being prepared, that the HVO -- or rather that the HDZ, who were becoming closer, according to the civilian and military sense, were preparing to take over full control of Vares municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you see a document in which this project was indicated, an order on the take-over of power in Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see the document at the time, but I saw it subsequently, after the act was actually carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us under which circumstances you saw that document and who had signed it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The document on the take-over of power in Vares was signed by the commander of the HVO, Borivoj Malbasic, and I saw it in the archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When was this document discovered? When did you personally see it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I personally saw that document a few days after the BH army units entered Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you give us the date when the BH army took over Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina took over Vares on the 4th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Since you have seen that document, could you tell us in a few words what the order consisted of and to whom it was addressed?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The order was addressed to units that had been designated for the take-over of power, and there was the military police there, part of the so-called sabotage units. It contained instructions as to the sequence of the take-over of individual buildings, starting from the civilian police, the post office, then the radio station, the Vares radio station, the municipality building, the social accounting service, the banks, and all the other facilities of importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When you were informed of this plan at the beginning of June, a plan that was to be implemented on the 15th of June, did you decide to take specific measures to oppose the implementation of this project?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My unit was based on the second floor of the police building, in an office of the former Territorial Defence headquarters, and the commander of the unit who was on duty at the time was given the task to strengthen guardposts being held by my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what happened to you on the 15th of June, 1992, around midnight?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Just before midnight, I received a telephone call from the president, Dario Andrijevic, to come to an emergency meeting, upon orders from Malbasic, in the premises of the police headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Who else did you see at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: At the meeting, there was Duznovic, Pejcinovic, Dario Andrijevic, Malbasic, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What did they ask of you during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: They asked me who had allowed me to reinforce guard positions held by my soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What did you answer, and what was their reaction?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I answered that I had done that on my own initiative, as I had received certain reports that something could occur; and in order to protect my soldiers, I had, myself, issued orders to reinforce security.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At the end of that meeting, what decisions were taken regarding you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was ordered to report to the command the next day, which was based in the Ponikve Hotel, and that I would be given orders to abandon the city, together with my unit, and to continue reconnaissance duties in the Nisici plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: This reconnaissance had do with the front line with the Serbs, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was to reconnoitre the rear of Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: How strong was your unit?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: My unit was formed, in accordance with the rules of the former Yugoslav People's Army, of Type 2, 45 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: How many soldiers?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Forty-five.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I see. Were there other units in addition to yours in the town of Vares in June 1992? I mean, other units of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Territorial Defence units emanated from the organisation of the Territorial Defence that existed within the framework of the former Yugoslav People's Army, and they were actually reserve forces. With the events in Sarajevo, those units were placed in combat readiness and were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, Mr. Mahmutovic. My question was, were there other soldiers of the Territorial Defence units in the town of Vares in June 1992 in addition to your own unit? That means were there only 45 soldiers, or were there more?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, that is just one unit that was in town. There was just that one unit in town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And the other Territorial Defence units, were they based outside the town?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: All the other units were located in local communities and in the barracks in Zabrdze.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question once again. On the 15th of June, 1992, your unit of 45 men was the only unit in the town of Vares for the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. You had already carried out reconnaissance in Nisici in the past?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Was it indispensable, in the case of Nisici, on the 15th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What kind of operations did you conduct at Nisici at the time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The first order we received from the staff commander, Borivoj Malbasic, was to reconnoitre the positions held at the time by the Serb army on the plateau, on the elevations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you remember that order of the 15th of June, 1992, to go to Nisici? You were being sent to investigate Serb positions; was that done with the purpose of getting you out of Vares?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I think that may well be a comment, Mr. Lopez-Terres. That will be for us to decide. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When you returned from Nisici, you spent 15 days -- that is, the 1st of July, 1992, when you came back to Vares with your unit -- and what did you find there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: There I found HVO units deployed along all the -- on all the positions that were already mentioned earlier, and ready for combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you note that the HVO had taken over the control over the town?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course I noted it, because one could not enter any office, not even the office where the communications centre was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Had a new mayor been designated for the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I tried to call by telephone some of the Territorial Defence representatives; that is -- but I could not establish contact with the staff. However, I learnt in no time that Mr. Anto Pejcinovic had already taken over the office of the mayor, of the municipal mayor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: But Mr. Pejcinovic was already there, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And the head of the police, was the chief of the police also replaced?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the former chief was replaced, and Ivica Gavran was appointed chief of the police -- civilian, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Pejcinovic, new mayor, did he bring in a new team to ensure the functioning of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Most offices in the municipality were taken over by new people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did some Muslims stay on the team?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That was so, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us, which offices did those persons hold?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, some Muslims did hold some posts in the administration. That was the health department, the education department, finances department, and I think civilian defence, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you think that those were the most important offices in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that those were the most important offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 1st of July, 1992, a new order was issued by Mr. Borivoj Malbasic regarding the Territorial Defence. Could you tell us something about that particular order?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was issued to prohibit the activities, the work of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you see that document with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because it was served on me, and I was advised that I could not be involved with the Territorial Defence any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 2nd or 3rd of July, 1992, the former mayor, Andrijevic, submitted his resignation, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he tendered his resignation, and I was present when -- to the legally elected deputy mayor, his resignation, the paper notifying his resignation. Her name was Mervana Hadzimurtezic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And after the 2nd or 3rd of July, 1992, did you see an announcement addressing the Croat population in Vares? Was there such an announcement there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Announcements were frequent at the time. Yes, at that time there was also an announcement calling all -- inviting all Croats to unite.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And at the same time, did the HVO in Vares decide to prohibit all the political parties but the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were -- all the political parties were prohibited, or any party gatherings, any party activities, were also prohibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were there also some announcements in the town that the HVO would not recognise the presidency of the republic in Sarajevo or the general staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Who were, according to these announcements, who were the individuals whom the HVO recognised as persons who had the authority to issue orders?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was the command and leadership line which led to Grude, or rather Kiseljak, Kiseljak, Central Bosnia, Busovaca, and others. It was that particular line. To speak about the direct line, I could not really say whether the command was in Kiseljak or Grude, but it was that -- that was the line of command and control, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: But I'm referring to announcements or posters which referred to Mr. Mate Boban or Franjo Tudjman. Were there any announcements, were there any posters or anything that would be referring to those two individuals?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was such a poster, with those contents, saying that they were accountable to Mate Boban -- or, rather, Franjo Tudjman, and that Franjo Tudjman was their president.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: As of July 1992, could you also observe some changes regarding the freedom of movement of Muslims in the municipality of Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certain changes did take place, especially as some persons -- some of the personalities of eminence, figures of eminence in the political life of Vares, were arrested. Then, as for the freedom of movement, one could not leave freely the municipality without special permits which had to be signed by Mr. Zvonko Duznovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Once this control was assumed by the HVO over Vares, was there also an order issued by the accused, Dario Kordic, which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If there's going to be a question about one of the accused, unless it's not in dispute, then the question should be asked in a non-leading form.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did the accused, Dario Kordic, in one way or the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, simply ask if he heard anything about Dario Kordic at this time. Mr. Mahmutovic, can you deal with that question, please?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I repeatedly heard about Dario Kordic as of the moment when he took over the office of the president of the HDZ onward. That is, I heard about him time and time again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you have any information on the basis of which Dario Kordic could perhaps issue orders regarding the take-over of the municipality of Vares, the control over the municipality of Vares?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stein?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Object to the form of the question. We're clearly in paragraph 49. He's trying to elicit at least one level of unreliable testimony from an individual who was not present. We don't know in the context that the individual received the information, whether the individual who received the information received it from other persons. It was received, apparently, after the events. We don't know how, where, when, the context, and all of that packaged into this witness. Therefore, on the basis of Rule 89(D) and (E), I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, will you inquire of the witness, please, how he heard about Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I was about to do it, but the Defence intervened just as the witness was about to tell us, and the objective of this is precisely to find out what he has to tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, first of all, before he tells us what he heard, how he heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Under what circumstances and from whom did you get this information about the possible role of Dario Kordic with regard to the take-over of control over the town, over the municipality of Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: There is an order saying roughly that the control in Vares should be taken over as soon as possible, and I believe it could be found somewhere in the Vares archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: But did you read that order personally? Or was it reported to you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that order after the BH army units entered Vares and I heard about the order from my officer who was responsible for the collection of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And what was the officer's name?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: His name was Nenad Gvozdenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So you are telling us that you first learnt from that person about the existence of that order, and after that you also could see that order for yourself?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Frankly, Judge, I plead surprise. In none of the papers given to us, the summaries of what the witness will say, the summary before you, which is before you now, that the scripts been followed, nor in the witness statement is there any indication that he ever saw, with his own eyes, this order. Everything that we've been led to believe thus far, was that he had heard about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stein, you can ask the witness about that in cross-examination, but the witness says that he saw the order, so he can give evidence of what it was that he saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (No interpretation)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have lost the translation. Can we find out, first of all, what it was that the witness saw on the document, the order?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It is a brief order saying that the HVO of Vares must take over all control in the territory of the Vares municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Who signed that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: There was Dario Kordic's signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) To round off this particular information, could the witness tell us under what circumstances did he see that order?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I saw that order in a part of the archive which was shown me, which was shown me in the municipality hall in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Excuse me. This is the archives that you already told us about when you said that BH army took over some of the documents on the archives when it took again the control of Vares in 1993; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. What I said was that a part of the archives was in the municipality hall, and I had access to it, and the mayor, Mervana Hadzimurtezic, and that text was then turned over to the archives. I don't know where it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: No. But my question was under what circumstances was this document disclosed, because you already mentioned some other documents before that.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. "Under what circumstances", I don't know what you mean. If you're asking me, "How you saw it?" I saw it on the table on which these documents that had been found in Mr. Pajcinovic's offices were laid out on that desk, and that's where I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I'm going back to what I asked. That document which was seized that you are talking about, and it was seized when the Bosnian and Herzegovinian army took over Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it wasn't seized by the army. It was the mayor who found it in her office, because the civilian authority entered Vares on that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So it was the mayor had left that town and left the documents behind; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) That was when, precisely? Could you tell us, when was that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: If you mean the document, when I saw it, I saw it two or three days after, so it must have been the 5th or the 6th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: We shall talk about Mrs. Hadzimurtezic, when she became the president of the war presidency. So this institution was set up and she stayed in Vares first, but then she left the town. And we shall now talk about two places that we already referred to in the beginning of your testimony, Strijezevo and Dabravine.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When Mervana was appointed the president of the municipality, the mayor, and after the events, that is, arrests and all the developments in the town, I decided to move out the Territorial Defence staff from the municipality of Vares and its civilian authorities. I decided to evacuate them to the village of Strijezevo. Then because of the weather conditions, I again evacuated these authorities to the village of Dabravine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the president of this institution, Mrs. Hadzimurtezic, did before she left Vares with regard to the bank account of the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when Mervana was appointed as the acting president of the municipality, she, as far as I know, did the following: At the social auditing service at the time, she changed the bank account number of the municipality and put her signature so that nobody could use that particular bank account except her as the mayor of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So the HVO could not draw the money from the municipal account?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Quite. That meant that nobody but Mervana could sign any order to draw money from that account.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The 26th and 27th of July, 1992, could you tell us what happened to you and some other individuals, members of the war presidency?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: In the night hours, that is, from the 26th and 27th of July, I received an anonymous telephone call that my arrest was about to take place and I should leave my flat. I did not do that because I did not think I had any reason, because I had not done anything, so that I stayed in my flat. Shortly afterwards, my doorbell rang and I was asked to open the door. I opened the door, and in the doorway or, rather, in the entrance, in the hallway of the building, there was the president of the SDA party, Avdija Kovacevic, and military policemen behind him, and then Zvonko Duznovic turned up and told me to get ready and that I was to go with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Then you were detained for several days in the Vares barracks; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From my flat, together with Kovacevic, I was taken to the barracks in Zabrdze, and I found there Mervana Hadzimurtezic, who had been taken into custody before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You said that you were not ill-treated, that you were only interrogated during those six days, and that the same held true of other persons detained there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can affirm that nobody laid a finger on me. But there were regular interrogations, not with any particular contents, not driving anywhere, but there were interrogations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Why do you think you were detained with other persons at the time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I still think that all of us who played a role in the Territorial Defence and all those of us who were arrested at the time, so both people from the command and from the civilian authorities, we were all arrested because they wanted to show us that we had absolutely no future there, that there were no prospects for us, and that we should not really do whatever we were doing because it was only nourishing illusions, I mean, it served no purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 6th of August, 1992, and a few days perhaps later, you were arrested again?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On my return from a neighbourhood community, and I was touring there a Territorial Defence unit on the way to Vares Meda, I was arrested and taken under custody at the command at the Ponikve Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At that hotel, who did you meet there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was taken there by the military police, and at that moment the commander, Borivoje Malbasic, approached me. He was visibly drunk. He had an automatic rifle on his shoulder. I don't know exactly how you call it, it was of Croatian manufacture, saying to me, "Didn't I tell you that you must not engage in any Territorial Defence activities, that that is all over?" Next to him was Emil Harak, who was acting chief of staff at the time, who said nothing. Then Malbasic angrily ordered his policeman to take me to the barracks and to lock me up in the basement. I was taken to the barracks, and I was tied up with -- handcuffed to the bed on the top floor of the barracks, so I wasn't taken to the basement after all. After that, early in the morning the policeman who was guarding me that night came in, untied the handcuffs, tied my hands behind my back, and escorted me to the room occupied by the commander, where Borivoje Malbasic himself was seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what Mr. Malbasic said to you at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Without looking at me, with bags under his eyes, he said to the policeman that he should untie me and leave the room. Then he stated that there was no time -- that he had no time to deal with me and that I had only two possibilities and that I had no choice, and that was to force Mervana to de-block the bank account or to face silent liquidation. I asked him to allow me to go to the Ponikve Hotel to collect my documents which I had left behind there. He called the policeman who was to escort me, and before that policeman came into the room, he said to me, "There is a third possibility, and that is for me to arrest you and, together with the documentation that I had collected reconnoitring the territory controlled by the Serbs, to hand you over to the Chetniks." Only then did I realise what it was all about, and it was a very big shock for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You decided to leave Vares at that point, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Going to my flat, I decided what I was to do and in which order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You asked a member of the war presidency to leave the town with you, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All the persons who had previously been arrested, I asked them to leave Vares together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the weeks that followed this encounter with Mr. Malbasic, the latter was replaced and moved to the region of Vitez, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was transferred from Vares to the municipality of Vitez. I think he was commander of one of the brigades there, but I don't know which brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, it's about time for the break, if that's a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. President, quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (No interpretation)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No translation so far.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Your Honour. Interpreter's fault. Didn't switch on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Shall we go on to the next issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) We have got to the year of 1993, specifically the second important point of Mr. Mahmutovic's testimony regarding events in Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, in the course of 1993, you said that there were no serious armed conflicts between the forces of the Bosnian army and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. There were no armed conflicts except for occasional provocations. One wounding, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: We come to the month of October, 1993, Mr. Mahmutovic. Around the 17th of October, 1993, is it true that five or six men, Muslim men from the village of Stupni Do, were arrested at the village of Pajtov Han that we mentioned at the beginning of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: A group of soldiers returning from Dabravine in a vehicle were arrested at the checkpoint in Pajtov Han. They were arrested, their vehicle was confiscated, and they were driven off towards Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us something in greater detail about these men? Which unit did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: All the soldiers came from the village of Stupni Do. One of them was the commander of a local unit in Stupni Do. His name is Mr. Himzo Likic. The others were members of that unit, and one of them was also a member of another unit of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You said that the unit of the Territorial Defence in Stupni Do consisted of some 50 members, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were that many men who were capable of participating in defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you please tell us a little more about the forces of Territorial Defence in Stupni Do, and specifically about the arms available to that Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence unit in Stupni Do, in addition to the forces I have just mentioned -- that is, in terms of manpower, consisting of some 50 soldiers -- as for armaments, it had light rifles, some automatic and some semi-automatic rifles, but the majority of weapons were hunting rifles. The unit was armed with some 40 barrels in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did that unit have a mortar?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It had one 60-millimetre mortar with eight shells, and a hand-held rocket launcher, and that was all, with a very limited quantity of ammunition, infantry ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you give us some idea of the amount of bullets per rifle?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: They had about 100 bullets per rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: These soldiers of the Territorial Defence of Stupni Do, were they wearing uniforms, and were they trained?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Very few soldiers wore uniforms because we didn't have the means or the resources to fully equip them. Most of them wore their regular civilian clothing. Some had some kind of uniforms made from military canvas, and they wore them, those of them who had them. As for training, the unit had no military training. By orders of the headquarters of the Territorial Defence, it was requested to provide circular defence of the village, to be able to defend it in case of an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: This Stupni Do unit came under your command as chief of the Territorial Defence of Vares municipality, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Stupni Do unit came under the command of the Territorial Defence, and under my command, as I was commander of the Territorial Defence headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Let us go back to the arrest of five or six men at the checkpoint of Pajtov Han in October. Could you tell us what happened to those men after they were arrested?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: After their arrest, those men were taken to the town of Vares. I saw those men for the first time after the army entered the town itself, in the area of Vares Majdan, where they had been left behind in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What was the condition of those men when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: They were in very poor condition. They were beaten up, with swellings on their faces. They could hardly move their arms because they were beaten on their arms. Simply speaking, they were unusable. And this applies in particular to Mufid Likic, who really did look miserable, who was in a miserable condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: This was only at the beginning of November, when the town was taken over, that you saw these men in this condition, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw those men on the 4th of November, around 11.00, to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Let us move forward to the 22nd of October, 1993. Is it true that you were informed by a military observer that unidentified vehicles were moving on the road between Kiseljak and Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: We received information from observers that some unidentified vehicles were moving from the direction of Kiseljak towards Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were you, yourself, able to note these vehicles transporting soldiers along that road, and from what position?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The BH army forces had their observation positions from which we received information. Together with the command of the tactical group, I went on the spot to check what was happening. We saw a number of vehicles moving from the direction of the so-called 30th kilometre towards Brgule, that is, the road from Brgule to Vares, and after that buses appeared and a certain number of trucks that stopped for a moment in the part of the road that could be seen from the Cemerska Mountain on the stretch of the road from the village of Sikulje to the village of Brgule. As the vehicles were at a standstill there, we saw that soldiers were coming out, and we saw that they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were you able to assess approximately the number of soldiers that came out of those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: We could not estimate exactly the number of soldiers. But judging by the number of vehicles, it was our estimate that there was some 200 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you learn eventually where those soldiers that you saw went?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Brgule was virtually the border of the area controlled by Serb soldiers and this access -- this direction that the vehicles went to, the vehicles that had stopped there, so that the only direction they could go to was towards Vares, and they moved in that direction. But we could no longer check that because of the wood that covered our field of vision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you receive confirmation a little later that HVO units had arrived in Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We received confirmation from a man who managed to leave Vares, and he confirmed that there was certain forces in Vares and what they were doing. Actually, the operation had already begun when the information reached us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were you able to receive any information regarding the original municipalities from which these forces came?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information, the forces arriving, the municipalities they came from was something that we could establish only later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us, which were those municipalities that you learned about later?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: They were soldiers, HVO soldiers, from Kiseljak, Kakanj, and I think also from Travnik there were some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 22nd of October, 1993, when those soldiers arrived in Vares, did the war presidency take a particular decision regarding the evacuation of the village of Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The war presidency subsequently decided, that is, in the course of the evening, that the civilian population of Stupni Do should abandon the village and start the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Was this order followed, in fact, by the civilian population of Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That order was not carried out due to certain reasons, because a similar such order had been given previously when it was carried out. But as then nothing happened, the inhabitants of Stupni Do returned to their village, and after that, when the second order came, they didn't carry it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us when the previous order had been given to the population of Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That order had been given when a report came about the arrival of some 500 combatants from Travnik, and that order was issued by the war presidency at the time, that is, for the civilian population of Stupni Do to be evacuated because they were virtually surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Yes, but could you tell us how much earlier that happened before the 22nd of October?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I think that was some 15 days previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the course of the month of July 1993, did the population of Stupni Do receive an ultimatum to surrender the weapons they had?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: At the same time as the inhabitants of Dastansko, the inhabitants of Stupni Do were also given an ultimatum by the HVO Vares to surrender their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did they, at the time, surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The inhabitants of Stupni Do or, rather, the unit of Stupni Do did not surrender their weapons to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were there any negotiations between the HVO and the population of Stupni Do regarding that ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Some negotiations were conducted between the unit command and I think it was called the council of the local community at the time regarding the surrender of weapons, but I think that nothing was achieved because the opinion of the superior command was requested and no decision was taken to surrender the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the evening of the 22nd of October, 1993, did you receive information confirming the risk of an attack against the village of Stupni Do for the next day?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Information reached us through the communications centre at the command position in Dabravine, the command of the tactical group received information that a certain person called Mato Mrljic had come to his sister Ana in Stupni Do and informed her that an attack was being planned against Stupni Do and that she and her husband should leave the village in order to save their lives. Mr. Alija Likic, Ana's husband, passed this on to inhabitants of the village in passing so that this report reached the person who took over the military powers, Husnija Mahmutovic, and he conveyed that message via communication links to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, meet the war presidency on the evening of the 22nd of October and discuss with them the possible measures to be taken in case of an attack against the village?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: There was a conversation, but at the time we did not confirm that the population should be evacuated. But the war presidency later on, in the course of the night, took the decision and, via Tomic, informed the president of the neighbourhood that the civilian population should be pulled out during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 23rd of October, at about what time and by which means were you informed of the attack on the village?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: According to the line of command of the Territorial Defence of Vares, sent to PDO 3 based in the village of Ravna, who was the first to inform us that something was happening in Stupni Do, in fact that the village was burning. This was early in the morning, about 8.30 or 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When you were informed of the attack, did you, yourself, contact representatives of UNPROFOR and other soldiers of the United Nations, and did you request that they intervene?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I personally contacted them, because the commander of the Operative Group East, having learned what had happened and since more information that Stupni Do was burning was confirmed by another observer group from another mountain, we contacted the UNPROFOR unit in Visoko and UNPROFOR units stationed in Vares. I think it was the Nordic Battalion that was stationed there. In spite of our attempt to persuade them and attempts of UNPROFOR forces to enter Stupni Do on that day, they were not successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 24th or 25th of October, 1993, you had a contact with one of the officers of the Nordic Battalion that you just mentioned, Major Egberg. Could you tell us about the conversation that you had with the gentleman?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: With Major Egberg, I had several contacts every day, endeavouring to persuade him that with his forces, he should enter Stupni Do and try to protect the population living there. Each time when the Major, with his unit, reached Vares Majdan and the road leading to Stupni Do, he was prevented by HVO forces from accessing and passing through. He would return regularly to his command position at Dabravine and report that he was virtually unable, doing anything, without provoking a conflict. Nevertheless, I was persistent and I appealed to him and told him the ways in which he might be able to reach some of the survivors in Stupni Do. I was convinced that it was not possible to kill each and every individual. Major Egberg did not succeed until three days later, when the first group of people from Stupni Do who had fled to the wood next to the Vares-Dabravine road, to collect them and bring them back to Dabravine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were you, yourself, able to meet one or several of those refugees and to talk to them about the attack on their village?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I met a number of them, those who arrived in large numbers. What I mean, the first group had about 15 persons on that APC and then one woman who managed to get out by herself, the one who saw when her son and her two neighbours were killed and then put in summer kitchen and set on fire. And that same night, I went to the village of Strijezevo, because that woman had passed through by Tohana where the HVO soldiers accepted her, gave her some food and water and saw her off to Strijezevo, so she had no trouble with the HVO soldiers in Vares and she safely reached her daughter's in Strijezevo. I talked to her that very night. I wanted to find out all that she knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that refugee, of that woman?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember the name of that woman. She's my aunt, and her name is Fatima Mahmutovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you know how many people were killed during the attack on the village?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: During the attack on the village, I know -- yes, I know the number: 38 persons lost their lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: As the attack proceeded, could you get the information from some other witnesses, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, from the military point of view, we more or less knew from which direction the village could be attacked, and that is what happened, indeed. Stupni Do was attacked from three directions, and it was confirmed later on from conversations with some people from the Vares HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you give us some indication, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Stupni Do was attacked from the direction of Vares Majdan, so Vares Majdan, the road towards Stupni Do. Stupni Do was attacked from another direction, Przici, the so-called junction, Stupni Do, and the village of Mir, Bogos, Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And that attack, how many men, how much materiel did it involve? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the forces that attacked Stupni Do were reinforced platoons, and I do not think that more than 100 men took part in the attack. At the same time, when there was attack on Stupni Do, all the males in Vares were being arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us something more about these arrests? When did they take place, and where did this population, this male population of Vares, where were they detained?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I said already, it took place at the same time as the attack on Stupni Do. They were detained in the gym of the secondary school, Ivan Goran Kovacic, in Vares, and the elementary school, Vladimir Nazor, in Vares, in the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: How many persons were arrested?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: From what I could infer from information, there were about 180 persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: For how long were they detained?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Those people were kept in prison until the forces of the BH army entered Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: That is, early days of November?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Between the event in Stupni Do -- that is, the 23rd of October -- until the 4th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you get some information about the attack on Stupni Do through Mr. Husnija Mahmutovic, who was the president of the village community?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Husnija Mahmutovic and six soldiers managed to get out of Stupni Do at night. That was the 24th -- 23rd to 24th November. In early morning, he turned up in the village Budozelje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did he tell you something about the intensity of the attack on the village?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I asked the command in Dabravine to urgently send a message that Husnija Mahmutovic and Mujcin Likic, another refugee from Stupni Do, should go to the command post in Dabravine so that the former could get the precise, the exact information as to what had happened in Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you know, where did the units which participated in Stupni Do come from?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The units came from Kiseljak, Kakanj. I already said in part, possibly, Travnik, and there were also attached units -- or rather attached men of the HVO Vares, those who agreed to take part in the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Who was the commander of Kiseljak units?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I know that the campaign was directly commanded by Ivica Rajic and his subordinates, those who carried out his orders. I also heard their nicknames. I don't know any one of them. One of the nicknames was, I believe, "Firga" , or something like that. Another one was called "Somo", or again, something like that. I mean, those are only the nicknames. I really don't know the names, who directly carried out the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At the time of detention of Mr. Ante Pejcinovic and Emil Harah, the commander at the time, do you know about the arrest?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I received this information after, from Borivoj Malbasic, who turned up at the negotiation on behalf of the HVO, when the attack was discontinued.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And that detention, the arrest of Mr. Prcinvic and Harah, the commander of the brigade, did it happen after or before the attack on Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Those arrests happened on the eve of the attack on Stupni Do, and that was when Kresimir Bozic was appointed the commander of HVO forces in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you know, if Mr. Pejcinovic and Harah were detained, how long were they in detention?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know when they were -- how long they were in detention, but I think, I believe, that they were in detention for two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I will now show you a document, Mr. Mahmutovic. It is a report by the ECM of the 2nd of November, 1993. I should like to -- this is a document which is part of the heap of documents that I shall refer to a bit later which you have received. This is a report of the 2nd of November, 1993, and it is 1.281. It could be the last document in the whole pile of documents. This is a document which is in English, as were most of the ECMM reports at the time. We should rapidly go through this document where it refers to the witness. The document says -- I hope everybody has it -- on the first page, last paragraph, it refers to Travnik, centre in Travnik. And he speaks about the member of the operational group of Bosnia-Herzegovina who is in Dabravine whose name is Okreh Mahmutovic; there seems to be a misspelling of Mr. Mahmutovic. Here it says that Mr. Mahmutovic, it would seem, explained to ECMM why, according to him, the massacre at Stupni Do took place. Mr. Mahmutovic indicated that Stupni Do was the local gateway to the territory controlled by the Serb Bosnians, and that it was thus a very lucrative place for smuggling and black marketeering. Again, according to this document, the residents of Stupni Do became reasonably well to do with this arrangement but had to pay a percentage to the HVO for all the goods, for all the merchandise which reached their place. In early October, the HVO demanded a substantially higher cut of the proceeds, and when the population of Stupni Do said no, the Kiseljak authorities -- rather the HVO from Vares, from Kakanj, decided, in response to that note, to conduct a coordinated attack on the village. Mr. Mahmutovic, this document, which refers to the period when you were there, seems to indicate, as a reason for the attack on Stupni Do, something which represents reprisals undertaken by the HVO against the local population of Stupni Do because the local population refused to observe the agreement which they had reached; that is, to pay them a particular share or tax, if I may call it that, which these HVO authorities requested from them, or rather demanded from them, from all the goods that were reaching the province. According to what this document says, could you please tell us if, to begin with, are you Mr. Okreh Mahmutovic who appears in this document, and secondly, do you also think whether these would be the reasons for the attack on Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not Okreh. I am Ekrem. It is true that I gave a statement in this form, and I believe that this statement -- whether it has to do with an awkward translation or something else, I don't know, but I never gave a statement in this form as presented here. I should say that they were not taking a percentage for the merchandise taken from Croats and Serbs in that commercial -- or contraband chain. It was a price increase in comparison with the early days when this smuggling chain, contraband chain, was opened.
