I stated to representatives that a possible decision to attack Stupni Do was made because Stupni Do was very near the town itself, the access to it is easy, it's simple, and Armija forces could not come to help, and some of the funds or some of the money which was turned over there, through the contraband, was the reason that the HVO forces which conducted the attack wanted to find a motive for the Croat citizens of Vares to leave Vares. I think that is the truth; that is, that that was one of the reasons, and that that is how it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Are you telling us today, Mr. Mahmutovic, that the report which is shown to you, and which was drawn by ECMM, is a misinterpretation of what you told them?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as I see it, because this could never be the only reason, and I think that what I have just said is one of the reasons for the attack on Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You mentioned several reasons, but what would be the chief reason for the attack, if it is not the version that we find in this report?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: One of the chief reasons, as I see it -- or as I saw it at the time, and now -- is setting in move the civilian Croat population from the Vares municipality. That is, they were trying to create some motive for -- to set on move this population. By killing 38 persons in Stupni Do, the motive was there, people were frightened, and the majority of Vares Croats set off without the Armija attacking them. They set off towards the hills and on toward Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So the Croat population was encouraged to leave Vares in fear of reprisals by the Armija, B and H, for the attack?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That is it, yes. I talked to many returnees, Croat returnees, in Vares, talked about these events, and everybody can verify it. Most of them left Vares fearing reprisals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the day when -- did the Croat population leave the town on the day of the attack on Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: According to the census, Vares was 22.000 population. About 12.000 of them were Croats, and after the Armija BH entered Vares, we noted that 751 Croats were still in Vares. Everybody else had left the territory of the Vares municipality. Some of them, yes, were kept in the area of Dastansko, which remained in that area until the cease-fire, until peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mahmutovic, for these explanations regarding the attack on Stupni Do. Let us now proceed to some questions -- move on to some questions regarding the accused. You said that you didn't know the accused Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You have never met, personally, Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I believe this morning you told us that Dario Kordic came to Vares several times. Could you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I can confirm it only on the basis of information I received from the town that Dario Kordic was in town. I heard it from my people who worked in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you know, whom did he meet in Vares when he came there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he usually came to meet with Anto Pejcinovic and the HVO leadership in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You explained that Mr. Kordic was an important representative of the HDZ party, and as such was responsible for military --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we are getting into a controversial area, and it would be better if the witness simply gave his evidence about this, about what he knows about Mr. Kordic, without being led in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) But the facts I wanted to mention come from the statement of Mr. Mahmutovic. That is, I was simply seeking some precision as to what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, could you tell us, what was the office held by Mr. Dario Kordic, as far as you know? You said he was an important representative of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: From media, from television, I heard -- that was when I heard of Mr. Kordic. I heard that he was appointed and designated the main member, but I don't know what it's called, of the committee of the HDZ for that part of Bosnia-Herzegovina. After that, one could see, and during the conflict, how Dario Kordic would appear as a reporter from the war theatres in Central Bosnia, so that from those media, I could simply follow the movements of Dario Kordic, and I therefore inferred that both the civilian and the military authority was in the hands of Dario Kordic for this part of Bosnia, rather Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So you believed that Mr. Dario Kordic had also a military office, a military function?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Since he signed various orders for HVO units, he must have also had a military office, military responsibility. If I remember well, in a report on television where Smiljko Sagolj communicated with him, it said "Colonel Dario Kordic".

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you personally see Dario Kordic, in a uniform, appear on these television programmes?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was the -- emerged a picture of Dario Kordic in a uniform. I think he had a jacket we just called a Spitfire, I believe, or something. It is a multi-coloured uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did Mr. Kordic have any authority over the HVO or over the municipality such as the Vares municipality, or Busovaca, Vitez, Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the control and command chain, I believe he did, because orders with his signature reached even Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you see some of his orders in these municipalities, issued to the HVO in these municipalities?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see some of these orders and Dario Kordic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity of meeting Mr. Tihomir Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: On two occasions. I don't remember the date, but after the fighting between the HVO and the army of BH ended, Mr. Tihomir Blaskic came to the territory of Vares, and the teams of the BH army and the HVO conducted talks there. In the group of the officers negotiating on behalf of the HVO was Tihomir Blaskic, and in the group which conducted negotiations on behalf of the BH army, I was the liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During those meetings, did Mr. Tihomir Blaskic mention in one way or the other the relationship particularly with regard to the command and control which would link him with the accused Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Objection. My grounds are that this witness is unavailable to us and we have no notice, up until the summary that I'm looking at, that this was going to be an issue in the case. This is nowhere in any of the witness's prior statements to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, that goes to the weight of the evidence, doesn't it, and it's a matter for cross-examination? Whether the evidence is admissible is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Correct. I'm trying to make those two distinctions, but I merged them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're satisfied these are all matters for cross-examination, and the evidence is admissible. I'm looking at the clock, Mr. Lopez-Terres. We're going to adjourn about five past or were going to adjourn at five past 1.00. Would this be a convenient moment or do you want to go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I believe we shall need 10 minutes more, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you could just go on and see how you get on. Deal with this bit of evidence, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You said that you met with Mr. Blaskic on two occasions after the signing of the Washington Accords, and during the conversations with Mr. Blaskic, did he indicate, in one way or the other, the relationship which he might have had with the accused Dario Kordic, any possible control and command chain, links of that kind?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was -- no, Dario Kordic was not mentioned in those talks. We were talking about separation of the forces of the army of B and H and the HVO and provision of conditions for more regular contacts and relations between the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Blaskic never pronounced the name of Dario Kordic in front of you during those meetings?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, on those occasions when I attended, those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Perhaps in some other circumstances?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I find your answer somewhat puzzling. –You seem embarrassed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: He's [indiscernible] on the evidence, and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Did Blaskic ever say anything to you about Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I have already said that Mr. Blaskic, during our talks, did not mention the name of Dario Kordic, as far as I could remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. That concludes that part of the evidence. We'll adjourn now. Mr. Mahmutovic, we're going to adjourn until half past 2.00. Could you please, during this adjournment and any others there may be, remember not to speak to anybody about your evidence? Don't let anybody speak to you about it, and that includes the members of the Prosecution. So don't, if you would, speak about your evidence until it's over. 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.05 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, let us go back to those two meetings that you had with Mr. Blaskic at the time you said that you met him in Vares. Did Mr. Blaskic tell you, in the course of those meetings, how he personally took his decisions and issued his orders?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Objection. This has been asked three times, and answered, and I believe Your Honour has ruled on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we'll move on, Mr. Lopez-Terres. The witness has said that he didn't on any occasion hear Blaskic talking about Dario Kordic, and I think that must be the answer. You can't go on cross-examining him on the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I was not asking about the accused's relationship with General Blaskic; I was just asking the witness whether General Blaskic, who was not "General" yet, how he, as head of the operational centre of Central Bosnia, issued his orders, how he prepared them and issued them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at paragraph 101, and it seems to me that the only relevance could be that paragraph. Shall we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I thought that perhaps there was a possibility of getting a little more information from the witness about the words of General Blaskic, because after all, he couldn't tell us what General Blaskic said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Lopez-Terres, please rephrase the question. It depends on the way you put your question. Could we know from the witness whether General Blaskic told him who gave him his orders, how he received his orders? Did General Blaskic talk to you, Witness, about the way in which he received orders, the origin of those orders? That is the question. Ask the witness that: Whether the witness received from General Blaskic any information concerning the orders he, himself, General Blaskic, received.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I have already said that at those meetings, we did not discuss those ways of conveying orders and commands, and that's very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do let's move on to something else now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Let us now talk about Mr. Ivica Rajic. Mr. Mahmutovic, you could tell us who, in your opinion, was the superior to Ivica Rajic in the chain of command of the HVO within Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that, according to our information, there was a command of the Operative Group Kiseljak which was under the jurisdiction of the next higher command, and that was the command for Central Bosnia, of which Mr. Blaskic was the commander, according to the military chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, did the accused Dario Kordic have any superior authority over Mr. Ivica Rajic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Within the system of control and command, he must have had, in view of the fact that in one of his statements on television, in answer to a question by a journalist, Sagolj, Smirko Sagolj, he said that he had still not taken any decision regarding the dismissal of Mr. Rajic because he hadn't investigated the circumstances regarding the accusation that Rajic had halted a humanitarian convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You are talking about a television broadcast during which the accused Dario Kordic answered to this journalist what you have just said. Did this broadcast take place prior to the Stupni Do event?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, the broadcast was shown during the time of the battles between the BH army and the HVO just prior to the events in Stupni Do. I think the battles were in Kiseljak, Central Bosnia, Vitez, somewhere there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: If I may intervene, my question was, in fact, whether the broadcast was shown before Stupni Do, and your answer was no. And later on, you explained, if I understood you well, that in fact the broadcast was shown before the events, unless there is a problem in the translation. But allow me to rephrase my question. The television programme that you mentioned during which the accused Dario Kordic told this journalist that he had still not taken a decision on the dismissal of Rajic, was this broadcast shown before the 23rd of October, 1993, or after that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was shown before the 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. President, Your Honours, at this stage of the testimony of Mr. Mahmutovic, I personally have finished with my questions which I intended to ask him. This morning I drew the attention of the court and the Defence counsel to several documents which I should like to tender into evidence. Let me specify that these documents were selected because it seems to me that they corroborate the events that the witness has spoken about on the one hand; that is, the first group of documents that I can come back to. The second category of documents which was compiled demonstrates the authority and the command of the accused Dario Kordic over officials of the Vares HVO that the witness discussed in detail. If I may, I could comment on these two categories of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, it may be helpful if you just take us briefly through the documents, announcing their numbers, which they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, quite. Regarding, first of all, the documents which corroborate the testimony of the witness, these are the following documents: Exhibit Z128 is a document dated the 10th of June, 1992. This document gives a permanent authorisation by Dario Kordic to a person called Vjeran Mijatovic, allowing him free passage throughout the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna to purchase weapons and food for the Vares HVO. I wish to point out that this document appears on page 11 in the chronology submitted to you by Prosecutor Nice. Therefore, in addition to corroborating one of the elements mentioned by the witness, and that is that the HVO at the time was purchasing weapons for its soldiers, also confirms the authority of the accused, because it is a document signed by him issuing orders and providing that authority for the purchase of arms for the Vares HVO. The second document that I should like to tender is marked as 144. It is a document dated the 1st of July, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It would be helpful if you actually went through it in the order that we have it, Mr. Lopez-Terres, because otherwise it will be difficult to go backwards and forwards. The next document I have is 139; perhaps you could deal with that next.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I apologise in advance, because these documents have not been put in the order in which I wanted to tender them according to these two categories that I mentioned. They were simply placed in chronological order, I think. So the first document has already been mentioned. As for the second document, Z139, it is a document dated the 23rd of June, 1992. It is a document which, in my opinion, demonstrates that it is necessary that the accused Dario Kordic had authority over the HVO of Vares municipality, to which on the 23rd of June, '92, he asked, together with Ignac Kostroman, that they provide various facilities for the Ilijas municipality. The third document that you have in this list is the one marked Z187. It is dated the 12th of August, '92. It establishes the authority of Dario Kordic over the officials of Vares municipality, Dario Kordic addressing an invitation to those officials to come to a meeting scheduled on the 14th, that is, two days later. Regarding the English version, there is an error. The meeting should have been held in Grude, the town of Grude, which is indicated there, and not as stated in the English text, in "Groups". In the B/C/S version, it is clearly stated "Grude", not "Groups". The next document that I propose to you is Z202, dated the 2nd of September, 1992, referring to Ivica Rajic, a document whereby Ivica Rajic indicates that Ante Pejcinovic and Borivoje Malbasic, two persons that the witness mentioned, should urgently report to Mr. Dario Kordic in connection with certain financial allowances. The next document that I should like to tender is document Z233, dated the 22nd of September, 1992. This document, which is signed, among others, by the accused Dario Kordic, indicates the conclusions of the meetings held in Central Bosnia, and on page 5 of the English version there's a paragraph referring to the municipality of Vares, indicating that the HVO has full control of power in that zone. This document is dated 22nd of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment. Let me make a note of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) The paragraph referring to Vares is on page 5 of the English document. I'm afraid the page numbers are not the same in the French version. I apologise to Judge Bennouna. It is page 705 of the French version. The next document I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before we leave that, I haven't got the passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: (Interpretation) It is on page 5 of the document concerning the municipality of Vares. Several municipalities having been mentioned. Vares is mentioned at the bottom of the page. Document Z233, the phrase in question that I underlined is as follows: "The HVO is in full control" in the English text. The next document that I am tendering for admission is Z229, dated the 30th of September, 1992, at 12.00, referring to a meeting organised and chaired by the accused Dario Kordic with members of the Kakanj HVO and in the presence of the president of the Vares HVO, Mr. Pejcinovic and Zvonko Duznovic, both of whom were mentioned in detail by the witness, the latter being the chief of security of the Vares HVO, the document in question being Z229. The next document is Z534. It is a document signed by the accused Dario Kordic and addressed to Messrs. Ante Pejcinovic and Zvonko Duznovic, again persons mentioned by the witness. It is dated 12 March 1993, and it is indicated and it says that the gentlemen from Vares can come for the prisoners early Monday morning. They should report to the brigade commander of the military police. It is again signed by the accused Dario Kordic. The next document that I am suggesting is a document dated the 30th of March, 1993, marked Z579, on which it is stated that the named Borivoje Malbasic named by the witness, who held the post of chief of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, the brigade coming from the region of Vitez that the witness also mentioned, the brigade of which Mario Cerkez was the deputy commander and in which Borivoje Malbasic is named as chief of staff. A document of the following nature is the following: 589, dated the 1st of April, 1993. Like the previous document, it is a document emanating from the Central Bosnia operation zone, that is, the headquarters of Colonel Blaskic at the time, and which again lists the various members of the Bobavaca Brigade, the Vares HVO Brigade, with names mentioned by the witness; Borivoje Malbasic, Emil Harak, Kresimir Bosic, and we also find Zvonko Duznovic. The next document again refers to events mentioned by the witness, that is, the limitation to the freedom of passage, freedom of movement. It is marked Z658, dated 15th of April, indicating that all vehicles and persons coming from Dabravine, that is, the town where the witness was, as well as the war presidency at the time, should be stopped by HVO forces. There are two final documents. Z1.146, dated the 19th of July, 1993, it is a document which demonstrates, if that is necessary once again, that Mr. Ante Pejcinovic was president of the Vares municipality HVO, and he signed this document called a political platform together with Zvonko Duznovic, who now holds the position of vice-president of the Vares municipality HVO presidency. The last document that I wish to submit, dated the 23rd of October, 1993, marked Z1.258, signed by General Milivoj Petkovic, referring to the termination of functions of Ante Pejcinovic, Zvonko Duznovic and Ivica Gavran, that is the time of the events in Stupni Do that the witness spoke about this morning. The final document in your pile is a document that the witness has already commented on. It is marked 1.281. It is a report of the ECMM on which the witness has already been questioned this morning. I have finished with the list of the documents which I am tendering into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, allow me to introduce myself very briefly. I am attorney Mr. Mitko Naumovski, one of the Defence counsel for Mr. Kordic. I have several questions for you. In view of the fact that we understand one another as we speak, would you be kind enough to wait a few seconds until the interpretation is completed and only then answer my questions? Mr. Mahmutovic, so far you have spoken several times with investigators of this Tribunal; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I gave two statements in Bosnia, and I spoke to the investigators here once here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: To whom did you give these two statements in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: To whom did you give those statements, to which bodies?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Those were the representatives of the Tribunal. There was a lady. I think that she was a police woman here from The Hague. And there was a gentleman there also, and I do not recall his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was this in March, 1996?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Probably so. This was sometime after the cessation of hostilities and the start of the proceedings, and this statement -- the last statement I gave about two weeks before my coming here, and this was just an amendment to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I would like you to be more specific. The first one you said you gave shortly after the cessation of hostilities. Can you please place it in time more specifically?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: This was, as has been written down, in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me, during that conversation, as I see here, according to the information I have, it took two days to complete this conversation.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It took a while to complete the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And you spoke by using an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. I do not speak English, so there was an interpreter there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The investigators took down notes based on the conversation that you had and all the subjects that you touched on?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I could notice, yes, they did take down notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The notes which were taken in March 1996 were also used during the interview you gave a couple of months ago, as you said; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this material was also used to complete the statement, because I had not completed the statement during the first interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me, when you spoke for the second time, you were given those notes for review?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Those notes were read out, and then some additional questions were asked, and I answered them, and then we finished in Sarajevo. It did not take very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we're in agreement that the statement which is the last one given, a couple of months ago, contains everything which had been taken down as notes by the investigators, and these were just amended by you during the last session?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is so, except that I gave some additional answer to the questions I was asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Please allow me to dwell a little bit on the statement you gave in December 1998, December 3rd. This statement has your signature in the English version. Do you recall signing it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The usher can show you the document. Is this your signature, Mr. Mahmutovic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. And this signature is affixed to each page of the document and at the end of it, and every one of these signatures is yours?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: At the end of this statement, I believe you will agree with me, it states that the statement had been read back to you in Bosnian, and that it contains everything which you said, according to the best of your recollection and memory?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let's first of all clear up something you said about Mr. Kordic. You said that when you had first heard of him, that this was a period when he had taken over as the president of the HDZ; you recall this? You said that today?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that this was broadcast on the media, that Mr. Kordic had taken over the position of the president of the HDZ for that area of Central Bosnia -- or perhaps even it is possible that he was the president of the HDZ for Bosnia and Herzegovina. There, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, this is exactly what I would like to clarify for the Trial Chamber: Do you exactly know when Mr. Kordic became president of the BH HDZ?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me ask you in another way: Were you sure that he was the president of the HDZ during the period which you referred to today?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: In the period that I referred to today, Mr. Kordic was president of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Today quite a bit was said about an order which you personally saw. This was -- you said that this was a very short order, and I'm quoting you: It says that the authority needs to be taken over in Vares. Do you recall it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Will you please tell us, you saw this order on the 5th or 6th November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You first heard of it from Nenad Gvozdenovic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What position was he in at the time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: He was in Dabravine. While I was a staff commander, he was assistant commander for security there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did he tell you where he saw this document? Where did he find it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It is not about him seeing the document, but when he was arrested in Vares, he learned that an order had been given to execute this order, to carry it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: After whose arrest?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Of Mr. Gvozdenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I must admit I do not quite understand you. You said today that you heard from your officer about this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you don't know where he learned about it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, because he learned about it in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So from a third, unknown, person?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Since he was engaged in security matters, he was also gathering intelligence, and then through the chain of command he reported that information to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell me, when you saw this document on the 5th or 6th November, 1993, you said that you had an opportunity to read through it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to quote the part, a short paragraph, which I then stated -- quoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what was the heading of this document? What did it say?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Usually all these documents have --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: No, no, no, I'm asking about this document specifically.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you a specific answer because it is a formal thing, who issues this order, a command, or an institution, that it does, and then at the bottom there is a signature of a person who had issued the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But for this specific document, you do not know what was in the heading part? That was my question to you.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me how many pages? Was this a multi-page document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was a single-page document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What type of paper was it? Was it an original?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was an A4-size paper, and I cannot answer whether it was an original or a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Whose name was signed?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Dario Kordic's name was typed up, and there was a longhand signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was Mr. Kordic's position also mentioned there? In what capacity did he sign it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know whether his position was also mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me, was this document -- regardless of whether it was a copy or an original -- stamped?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: There was a stamp on the left-hand side -- left of the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber, what stamp was it? What body, which body was it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you this because I did not notice it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether this document also had a registration number or a log number in the heading, something that would be easy to trace down, to trace it down to its source?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it had a -- next to the heading was another stamp, a registration stamp, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And whose stamp was it, what body?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, I did not know what body it was. I just read the order, and I saw the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me, you said that you saw this document, that it was shown to you in an office, in an archive. Where was this? I wasn't clear on this.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: After the BH army entered Vares, two days later I visited the president, Ms. Mervana Hadzimurtezic, and Mr. Pejcinovic had been there before, as you know, and in the office there was a whole pile of these documents. Through conversation with her, I was only able to peruse through some of these documents, because all the documents which were found there were turned over to the security service of -- I don't know whether it was civilian or the military police in Vares which had started operating there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, you said that the last statement you gave, that you had given it to the best of your recollection. This is what you said. We do not have your first statement because it only exists in notes?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the statement, and to this day, I say that whatever I can say with precision is what I remember, and my only objective is really to find out the truth before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) With your permission, Your Honours, I would like to show the witness the only statement which we have of 3 December, 1998. I have sufficient copies for Your Honours and for all the parties.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D31/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) The usher can put the statement on the ELMO, and I will guide the witness as to the Bosnian version. Your Honours, what I would like to refer to is in page 5 of the English original.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, would you please turn to page 5 of the translation which was given to you by the usher. It is at the bottom of page 5, the last couple of sentences.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, page 5. Page 5, fifth paragraph, last sentence in the English original.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, in your statement signed by you personally and which I have shown to you and which I would like you to follow what you say, in relation to this -- quote, unquote -- putsch: "I have heard about an order given by Dario Kordic and addressed to the HDZ/HVO Vares to take over the power and control in Vares. I have never seen this order personally, and I learned about this later."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We haven't found it yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation)

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, I said what you said, to the best of your recollection, as you said, to the investigators, and was my reading of it correct? Is that correct, Mr. Mahmutovic, what I read? Was it read correctly?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was something like that. Maybe not the same order of words, except the thing which says "I learned later on about it." What I said is that I saw it later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that you said what you said to the best of your recollection, and you now confirm what I have just read, which is that you never saw this? In other words, this is a crucial difference, the difference between what you are saying now, today, and what you said in March 1996 and in December 1998. You never mentioned that you ever saw it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: It states here that I have never seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that you signed it as your own statement, that Their Honours saw that every page of this statement, which is in English in the original, every single page is signed by you; then this is a true translation?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: This could be an error in translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Oh, so you see this as an error in translation? You had not a single objection at the end of the -- before you signed the record of this translation?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The way it was read to me, I had no objections, and I think that this was not -- this is not what I said, and it wasn't translated to me this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Could, then, somebody please help me to translate what you said? Perhaps we can ask the interpreters to translate what it says in this sentence, which is the last sentence in paragraph 5. Could the translators please interpret to the witness the sentence starting, "I have never seen this order personally, and I learned about it later on"? So this is the interpretation of what I have just read to you and which has been stated and written down and which is signed on every page of the statement and which you said that you gave to the best of your recollection. Do you agree that what I read to you is correct and that it was signed by you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I accept that it was signed, but I do not agree that this is what was said in translation to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mahmutovic. We can move on to something else, but perhaps just one additional question, when we're still dealing with documents: Towards the end of your testimony today, you said that there were some other documents which you personally saw and which were signed by Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in what capacity did he sign them? Was it in the same capacity, or what capacity was it, these documents which you saw signed by him?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Those documents were signed in the same capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell us what capacity this was?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I said that I could not specify what capacity this was, what position he was in, because the chain of command was centralised. In other words, it was issuing from the same military and political source.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I understand that as your conclusion rather than as your first-hand knowledge.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: If that is your understanding. I believe in fact I did not have an obligation to find out in what capacity he had signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were the documents which you saw also some kind of, how shall I call them, military orders?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: For the most part. There were also some calls, there were some transfers of command authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: They were all signed by Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were all signed by Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: No, but I'm referring to his capacity. Did he sign it as a person or on behalf of a certain body? In which position did he sign?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you an answer to that, because I really do not know what position he was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go back to the beginning. I'm going to take you back to the beginning of your testimony today. I heard you say that you studied political science, but I'm not sure whether you had ever graduated.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, this was -- I graduated from it in Sarajevo. It was supplementary education.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When was it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: This was 1984, and I did it while working.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What was your title once you graduated?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The title that I acquired was -- I think it was something like senior political scientist.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Is that something like a two-year course?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What is your basic profession, if I may ask?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I am an engineer of mechanical engineering.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In the former Yugoslav state, you were a member of the Communist Party?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member until it dissolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber when this took place in time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot frame it in time because we just -- they were transformed into the SDP, the Socialist Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In the elections of 1990, were you a member of the SDP, of the Social Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: One more question. When you completed the school of reserve officers, you were given a rank?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, you weren't given a rank there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You are confirmed a rank by decree?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What was that rank when you went back to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't go back to Vitez. I went to Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, when you went back to Vares.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was a lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When did you join the TO?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The moment I came back from the school, I joined the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What was your highest rank in the TO in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was captain first class in which I was -- a rank which I was conferred in '83.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What were your duties in the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was assistant commander for politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were you in this position until the elections of 1990?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was in this position practically until it was dissolved following the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said that it dissolved, that the staff was dissolved?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was dissolved after the parties, the winning parties, agreed to it. If I may add, the HDZ and SDA wanted to reform it or re-establish it. In other words, they wanted to see the SDP pushed far away from any control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Now we're talking about 1990?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: It was still bound to JNA?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Until the new parties took over the power.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When was this, if you can tell us specifically?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Immediately after the elections and after the election results were announced.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In your statement, you talked about the percentages of population in the area of Vares municipality. I would like to ask you a different thing. Would you agree with me that after the elections, the municipal assembly had 50 deputies?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Nineteen of those were SDP members, 13 HDZ, nine SDA, eight of the so-called Reformists or the Markovic followers, and one the youth organisation led by Kares. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, I didn't count, but it sounds about right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Trust me, I counted them.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I trust you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Based on these electoral results, you said that Andrijevic -- is that his name?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: That Dario Andrijevic was elected mayor of the town, Zvonimir Dugonjic was president of the executive board, Dario Andrijevic was SDP and Zvonimir Dugonjic was from HDZ?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Then again they had their own deputies. Ratko Gajic was deputy of Dukovic, who was another Serb from the SDP, and the deputy of the mayor was Mervana Hadzimurtezic, who was for SDA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I also had noted that the assembly formed the joint defence staff in 1992. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Not on the -- I think it was on the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Are we thinking of the same thing? So the joint staff of the HVO and the TO, I have a number of names noted down here, those who were active at the time, and they include Emil Harak, who started in the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it was called the municipal headquarters of the Territorial Defence rather than the word that you have just used.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who was the commander or the chief, whatever, of this municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borivoje Malbasic was then appointed the commander of the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the former commander, the former commander, was replaced because his subordinates were not happy with him?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That was the official account of it, that it was because of the discontent of his subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But wouldn't you agree that it was supported by the HVO and the TO, I mean his replacement?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, I forgot to ask you in the beginning, you told us that you were the vice-president of a new party, and that is the Party for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And is Mr. Silajdzic the president of that party; you told us that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Court if your party had a coalition with the SDA party in the elections?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the last elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Today there was also talk about ethnic groups beforehand, I mean it must be prior to the elections, do we agree, and we know it only too well, that at the time that we're talking about, that is, in the former Yugoslavia, there was practically only one party, and that was the League of Communists; there were no number of parties? We agree about that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it was. Thank you. When you told us about Mr. Malbasic, who became the commander of the joint staff, you said he came from the SDP, he was nominated by the SDP or, rather, he was a member of the SDP?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said, and that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You also said that the HVO formed its forces outside the TO. Could you please tell us when was that? When did the HVO begin to do that or, rather, at what time did it come about?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, with the formation of the military police and the insignia of the HVO, which were then put on, was when the units of the HVO began to be formed, and with them we absolutely had no communication. We had nothing to do with them. And one of them was the unit of the civilian police. That was formed, too, and a special task or a subversion, sabotage unit, or something like that was also formed. We called it BDO. So it so happened that in the Vares municipality, neighbourhood communities were rather pure ethnically, so all the units that were formed on the basis of the territorial principle and by the order of the former Yugoslav army were, to all intents and purposes, were set up and thus they were then incorporated in the HVO or the units of the Territorial Defence, such as they were at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Right. But tell us, please, in the municipality of Vares, there were also several Serb villages such as Brgule and others, and those villages were the first ones to proclaim themselves parts of the municipality of Vares, that is, they seceded from the Vares municipality; is that true?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they seceded. And I think they even set up some kind of borders which had the Serb military region of Romania or something, so that was their territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And that was accepted tacitly, if I may say so, in the rest of the Vares municipality?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it was tacitly accepted. I had rather said, "one couldn't but accept it." There was no other choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, were there some other villages in the Vares municipality which did not secede and yet where the JNA brought weapons. I think it was Planica?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, so this was the village of Planica and Brad. Those two villages moved out subsequently after the HVO attacked the village of Planica, and seized weapons. And then gradually the population began to move out of those villages and everybody left, so that there was nobody there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell us if your unit, that is, as you called it, the reconnoitring platoon or the anti-sabotage unit, did it have anything to do with the seizing of weapons which the JNA brought into those villages?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. My unit was, at that time, in a different place, and we were tasked with the reconnoitring in the directions that I already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, at the time when you headed this subversive or, rather, the anti-sabotage unit, were you also the assistance to the commander, Malbasic, I mean?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You had absolutely no duties in that staff?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, but as the unit commander, I was directly subordinate to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Today it was also said that the HVO procured armaments for its forces, and tell us, in the municipality of Vares, we have this joint staff. Weren't the weapons procured for both sides I mean jointly?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The Vares tier, either within this joint staff or outside it, did it ever get any weapons from Croats, either from the area or from outside the area of Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, until joint action against the army of the Republic Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That was towards the end of fighting for Nisic/Visero plateau in '94 and '95.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And in '93 and '92, you were procuring weapons on your own account?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say it was armament. We mostly used what we had, what the people had. Those were mostly hunting weapons and a few automatic rifles that people purchased themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Right. But if I understood you properly, you had communications centres, you had radio stations and all that. All this is specialised equipment that has to be obtained from somewhere, so you did?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. Communications, that is, we seceded to them from the joint staff and then it was distributed. It was divided according to the principle which governed the distribution of what formerly belonged to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But the former TO, to which superior command was it attached?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Formerly, to the regional staff of the Territorial Defence, with the headquarters in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So it was to Sarajevo's. You did not have a regional centre?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. There was only a regional centre for the training of commanding officers of the TO in the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Just one more question on this subject. When did you cut any communication with this superior command in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was on the 6th of April, '92, when I requested the assistant commander for political work, Mr. -- the gentleman was in the command of the regional staff, occupying the same office, and I simply asked him, "What are we to do under the circumstances?"

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So if I understand you, it was three days before the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina decided to abolish the republican staff of the former state?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know the date exactly, but I know that telephone lines were still in order, so that that was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Today you devoted a few moments to Zvonko Duznovic, explaining his office and the man and so on and so forth. You said that he, in a radio broadcast, he said there could be no cohabitation with Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was that. Yes, he did pronounce those sentences, and radio broadcasts, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did he speak in his own name?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps in his own name, but I had no way of knowing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you because we heard from you today that Muslims shared in the HVO government, and you gave us also the cabinets, the offices they held, but I don't remember you telling us -- Mr. Mahmutovic, you understand that there are two HVOs, the civilian HVO, responsible for the civilian authority, and the military HVO, and that is the army; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I know and I feel that that was one authority, to all intents and purposes, both the civilian and the military I think as one. I did not feel it otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you think that the HVO is only one, that there are not two components or, rather, several components to it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Today you told us that you say that some Muslims discharged some unimportant duties in the HVO government. You mentioned education, health care and finances, but that one couldn't consider as unimportant, could one?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: If you want my opinion, they are unimportant officers because they had no say in the final decisions taken by the government. They were simply individual portfolios, and they were accountable to those who were important in the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But still, those people who discharged offices in that government, you will agree with me that among other clerks, if I may put it so, there were still Muslims, that is, Muslims who had worked in the municipal government before?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I believe there were some, yes, but mostly people who were accountable to gentlemen from the HVO or, rather, the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But that is only your inference?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I'm asking about facts. After the HVO took over the power, there were also -- in that power, there was some offices held by Muslims, and among the rank-and-file civil servants, if I may call them that, there were also some Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When was the war presidency formed? I didn't hear you properly.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The war presidency was formed immediately after Dario Andrijevic and Ms. Mervana Hadzimurtezic submitted their resignations. So the power was taken over the 1st of July, and this could have been there for a few days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Today you told us, if I may repeat it, that to all intents and purposes, Mervana Hadzimurtezic automatically became the president of the war presidency.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how you understood me, but it couldn't have been automatic because everybody resigned and she had to seek consent of the president of the presidency to take over that duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I do understand what you are saying, but what I want to say is that Dario Andrijevic did not ask for any authority from the assembly -- from the presidency, because the assembly was the one which elected him, so she should have also asked the assembly?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the assembly could not meet, and that must have been the reason why she sought the consent of the president of the presidency to take over, because Dario Andrijevic submitted his resignation to her, I mean the one which I saw, and I was present there when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yeah, right. But when you told us about that bank account, she changed the names of signatories of these accounts without again seeking the approval of the assembly or any other body?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the statute of the municipality, under such circumstances, which were the state of war, actually, the war presidency was to be established, and she did that, and she formed that war presidency, and I'm not sure, but I think she had the approval of the presidency to change the signatories; that is, to change those persons who would be authorised to draw money from that account.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, this war presidency, could you tell us about the ethnic structure, the majority of them?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The majority were the Bosniaks. The Muslims prevailed in that war presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, we are now talking about the HVO government, and you lived there at the time, so you should know: About 2.000 ex-police arrived there, about 1.200 Muslims and about 800 expelled Croats arrived in your municipality. Would you agree with these figures?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with these figures, but -- because while I was in Vares there were no refugees, only the refugees from East Bosnia were passing through Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that very many refugees passed through Vares, but I was going to ask you who took care of them, who looked after them when they arrived. Was it that government that was there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I'm repeating that while I was in Vares, there were no refugees there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But they were passing through, you say?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were passing through. They were not stopping there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So who were the first refugees who stopped in Vares? Those from Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, I think that the first refugees came from the area of Sokolac and that part of -- that part of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I think they arrived sometime in early August, or perhaps early September. At that time I was not in Vares any longer, so I just don't know how many of them there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But were there Muslims or Croats?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I think there were both Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: To round off this part, and they were accommodated in Vares, they were offered some basic assistance there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were accommodated in Vares and villages around it. I know that in Stupni Do, there was a certain number of refugees from East Bosnia, Muslim refugees from Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Right. Let me ask you something else now. You explained to the Court that you formed the war presidency, that later on you moved first to Strijezevo and from there to Dabravine, but that did not mean that you split up in territorial terms, if I may say so? First the Serbs took out some villages and joined the Serb part of the Ilijas municipality, and now we have also Croats and Muslims somehow separating, parting company in territorial terms; is that true?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I do not think that this is a correct postulate, and I can tell you why: Because there were no demarcation lines drawn between the Armija and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, we must take care of the interpreters. No, that is not what I mean at all. I do not mean those lines. What I mean is territories. You were in one part of the municipality and they were in another part of the territory. Your command was in Dabravine and the Croats had it in Vares; that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That is how it was, but mostly for security reasons, to avoid any possibility of the HVO arresting us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But before that happened, you commuted to work in Vares? I didn't mean you personally; I meant the mayor, lady mayor, rather, the deputy -- deputy president of the assembly, Mervana, and others, while the roads were open?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I mean after you had set up your command, or rather when you still had the TO, before the war presidency was formed, you went there to perform your duties and went back. That is, you could enter Vares?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, until the 6th of August, '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: That is what I meant, yes. You spoke about some posters which turned up in Vares. Could you please describe one of those posters, the size of them? What did the heading say?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was the A4 paper sheet size, must have been copied on an old-fashioned machine, and then one could have it, and they were put up in public places where one usually put such things, posters in times of elections, or any kind of that material would be affixed. The heading of such announcements or communications, it said "HVO, Vares," and the signatures varied, depending on the matter at hand. As the rule, Ante Pejcinovic, and at times Zvonko Duznovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You mean they were the ones who signed those posters?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I guess there must have been several kinds. Some of them must have been some practical instructions or something like that, warnings?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were those too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you were referring to the other kind, you said, with some publicity messages or something like that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes. Simply that kind of an attitude, showing the attitude towards Muslims in that town, and because of their nature, they were noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You spoke about Ante Pejcinovic. Do you know -- would you know -- but do you have any immediate knowledge, who did he communicate with from the superior structures, from the superior rungs of the hierarchy? Who was he linked with?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, part of the communication going from Vares would go through the territory of the neighbourhood community of Dragos and Mikovice, where the units of the Territorial Defence were stationed. We always had information when Mr. Anto or one of the Vares HVO leaders would go to Kakanj, that is Catici, and who they met, who they talked to. I believe that in his report, or in a newspaper article he published, he described it in full, and I don't want do change it, because he said how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking whether you knew: Whom did he communicate with?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he communicated with Dario Kordic, and at times with Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I'm asking you, did you have any direct knowledge, do you have any direct knowledge about that? Directly, immediately, not the conclusion that you draw or what the newspapers say, but do you have any personal knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: My personal knowledge is through my men, who often negotiated with the gentlemen from HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But that is again according to other people?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, officers placed in charge in that, and politicians who were charged with conducting the negotiations with the HVO to avoid conflicts in Vares, because one always had to consult with somebody to see what needed to be done and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So all that you know, you've heard from others. You don't have any personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: That is what I said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned today that Zvonko Duznovic personally issued car permits to enter or leave the municipality, but did that also apply to the territory within the municipality?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, anyone who wanted to leave the territory controlled by the HVO had to go to Zvonko Duznovic and obtain that car permit if he wanted to leave the town, or rather, that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But after August of '93 -- that is, '92, did your side also introduce this measure? That is, trying to restrict the communication, that is, departure from the municipality and so on and so forth? In other words, would you agree that your men also needed a permit if they wanted to get out of the municipal seat or go beyond the area which was under your control?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you did need such a permit to leave the territory or municipality. You just couldn't move around unless you had a paper, a passport or something, a paper issued you. But at that time you did not need this for the territorial municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But who issued that authorisation to leave the municipality?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was an agency of the municipal government. I believe it was the secretariat for national defence. I believe that is what it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You described your conversations with Malbasic about your arrest and so on and so forth, and you said that he offered you two possibilities, and then adding a third, that he would deliver to you the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But all of a sudden, then, you were released, were you not? You were simply released, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was released, and they met my request. I could go to the Hotel Ponikva, where the HVO staff was, and to take out all the people -- everything that was there. And I was taken from the Hotel Ponikva to the town of Vares itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So in spite of the threats that he made, you were simply released, without any further requirements made on his part?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. I'm telling you things as they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Let's just make these things clear. Today, you mentioned the event when in Pajtov Han, on the 17th of October, '93, those soldiers from Stupni Do were arrested, six of them, I think it was. But -- never mind. There's something else I wanted to ask. Could you tell us when this barricade was put up by the HVO in Pajtov Han, or rather, when did they withdraw to that position?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: The HVO formed that position, or checkpoint, as it was called, I think it was in September 1992, after an event which, if I may be allowed, I could tell you about --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, my question was when, and then comes the question why -- of course, with Their Honours' permission. I would like you to tell us about it. I think that Their Honours agree, so tell us: Why did they withdraw to that position?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Certain organisational problems occurred regarding passage to the village of Budozelje and Strijezevo, and following my orders, we put up our own group to control that part of the territory. Immediately after this group of mine was positioned there to control the area, Ante Pajcinovic came up with a request, together with Zvonko Duznovic, that we should urgently organise a team, without my presence, which would go to Vares to negotiate the question of the formation of this checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: If I understand you well, you were actually adopting positions, both you and the HVO police?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Having mentioned Dabravine, may I just add a few words to what I've just said? I think it will make things clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I think this was quite sufficient, because my question had to do with this checkpoint. I don't think there is any need for any further elaboration. I should like to remind you, if you remember, that incident in connection with HVO tanks.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Please, I think this is important, for me to explain why developments in Pajtov Han took the turn they did. So please allow me to tell Their Honours about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, a meeting was held in Vares municipality building between representatives of the army and the mentioned gentlemen of the HVO, and an eight-point document was drawn up, and one of those points was that there should be no forces in that area controlling the area, so that freedom of movement would be ensured in all directions, both for the HVO and the TO. However, Zvonko Duznovic, the very next day, after the TO units' withdrawal from that area -- that is, the area of the Vares slaughterhouse -- the army withdrew, and Zvonko Duznovic reinforced and positioned his forces at the very crossroads to the village of Budozelje, the mouth of a small river there. When we asked him why he had done so, he said that he did not agree with what had been signed and that he had been tricked into signing that document. This shows that the HVO checkpoint was reinforced there, and for as long as that checkpoint existed, we could not reach the units of Strijezevo and Budozelje by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, can I continue with my questions?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I wanted to remind you, of course, if you remember, an incident linked to oil tanks of the HVO in Dabravine. Do you remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I do. Tank lorries of the HVO had permission from the command of the BH army in Zenica. They had permission to pass. However, those lorries were stopped.
